recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11125 unless a work group wants a new substantive model for requisitions beyond this historical resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-11125 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification OO issue raised against DSTU2 DiagnosticRequest and the Request pattern. It asked whether requisition information needed more detail than an Identifier; the accepted modification was not to add a requisition resource or object, but to add Request guidance that comments shared across a requisition should be represented as Observation or Communication and linked to the relevant requests through supportingInformation.
initial_application: The original workflow source commit 839bf586d6 explicitly included #11125 in a broad workflow batch and added a Request compound-requests section with the shared requisition-id discussion and the implementation note directing common comments or notes to Observation/Communication linked through Request.supportingInfo.
additional_context: DiagnosticRequest is no longer an active resource in this checkout; source/fhir.ini lists ServiceRequest as active and DiagnosticRequest under removed resources, while ServiceRequest.requisition maps to Request.groupIdentifier and ServiceRequest.supportingInfo maps to Request.supportingInfo. Later FHIR-38868 changed stale Request.requisitionId wording to Request.groupIdentifier on the combined branch, preserving the requisition business concept while aligning with the current Request pattern element name. Community searches found no Zulip or Confluence record that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active Request notes already say that common comments or notes spanning a requisition should be captured as Observation or Communication instances linked to relevant Request instances using Request.supportingInfo, which is the requested applied resolution expressed in current element names.
